Keep every one of them, spelled exactly as in English, braces included. Never translate the word inside the braces. You MAY move a placeholder to wherever your language needs it in the sentence.
meta.control_name_notes: Where an English string names a control, it names it in one of two shapes. A single control is written as its label followed by the widget word: "press the Calculate button", "the Recalculate automatically setting", "the Required fire flow box". A menu path is written as comma-separated labels: "File, Save as"; "Settings, Calculation, Hydraulics". In BOTH shapes the label is another key's value. Translate it with exactly the words you used for that key, so the sentence still names what is on the screen; translate the widget word and the surrounding prose normally.
meta.glossary_notes: glossary lists the technical terms that the strings in this batch use, each named in plain words, with your language's preferred translation where one exists. meta.context_notes: Use key_context[key].neighbors to keep register consistent with nearby translated strings. key_context[key].tip is the help text shown for that label, and key_context[key].label is the label a tip explains: read the pair together, and give the same thing the same word in both. Where the partner already has a translation in your file, its value is shown.
meta.plain_notes: key_plain[key] says in plain words what that one string means, other wordings joined by "or". Use whichever your language expresses most naturally and compactly; you are not bound to the literal English wording.
meta.key_notes_notes: key_notes[key] are notes about that one string: how much room it has, symbols to keep exactly, what it refers to. Follow them. They are instructions to you, never text to put in your file.
meta.suggestion_box_notes: Read suggestion_box and follow it. It is part of your instructions, not a footnote: a sprint does not close while a translator complaint is unanswered.
translator_notes: Tree, parent, child and inherit are the words of a family tree. Use the everyday family words of your language.
meta.translator_notes_notes: Read translator_notes and follow them. Each is true of every string you translate.
meta.concept_notes: Read concept_source and follow it. key_concepts lists, for a key that names a concept, its plain-words name, which is what you translate from; English is one rendering of it.

suggestion_box:
## Suggestion box — file a grievance about the English

If any English string made you guess, file it. You are the only person who will ever
notice, and a string that made you guess will make the next 25 translators guess too.

File an entry when: the English has more than one plausible reading; a verb or adjective
has no stated object; a word's intended sense is not its most common sense; a term maps
onto a dangerous second sense in your language; a claim in the text looks false or stale;
or the tooling handed you a preferred_translation that is wrong for the context.

Report them in your final message as a JSON array, separate from your prose:

FRICTION: [
  {"key": "<lang key>", "complaint": "<what made you guess, in one sentence>",
   "readings": ["<reading you chose>", "<reading you rejected>"]}
]

An empty array is a fine and useful answer. Do NOT invent entries -- a false one costs a
human's attention. But do not stay quiet to be agreeable either: this channel exists
because real complaints were previously buried in prose and never acted on.

Where it goes and what happens next: the orchestrator copies each entry into
dev/english-friction/<sprint>.json, adds "source": "translator" and "lang": "<your
language code>", and answers it with a "disposition" plus a written "resolution" --
english (the English was rewritten), intent, glossary, dismissed (with the reason), or
refer-to-human. refer-to-human is a real answer and does NOT close the entry: escalating
is not resolving, and it stays visible until Tom rules on it. friction_check.php blocks
the sprint from CLOSING while any entry of yours is unanswered, so filing one is expected
work that the sprint waits on -- not a complaint about the sprint.
concept_source:
## Concepts are the source

Each concept is named in plain words, with its synonyms joined by "or". That plain name
is the authoritative source; the English term is one rendering of it, as yours will be.
Where key_concepts lists a concept for a key, translate the thing the plain name
describes, and give that concept the same word in every key that cites it. Where a
concept also has a definition, it is the author's own and outranks everything else.
Where a key has no key_concepts entry, the English is the source, as before.

uniqueness_attention lists the few groups of concepts that sit side by side on one
screen. Find unique names for each.

The list at the left of the box jumps to a section or a sub-heading. The sections are Symbology (Node labels, Node colors, Link labels, Link colors, Customer, and All), Map, Page, Assets (ID prefixes, Values, and Custom properties), Calculation (Solver, Units, Time, Hydraulics, Energy, and Quality), and Credits. keys_to_translate.lpn_guide_rr_what_def: Choose Water, Reports, Solver (run). The Solver (run) report is the printed report of a run in the layout and wording of the EPANET report. It starts with that header and the name of the network, then counts the junctions, reservoirs, tanks, pipes, pumps, and valves, then states the analysis options, and then lists the hydraulic status of the run with its warnings. The Copy button copies the text.

keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_1_def: By default the network is solved by the EPANET solver. When a total run time is set, each reporting time step is calculated in sequence: tanks fill and drain, demands follow their patterns, and the toolbar plays back the run. With Use the built-in solver selected, the network, including an extended period simulation and an EPANET-MSX analysis, is solved by the built-in solver instead. Input that EPANET does not accept is not accepted by the built-in solver either, and the status bar reports it.

keys_to_translate.lpn_engine_needed_failed_why: The EPANET solver could not be loaded, so the built-in solver runs this network. {reason}
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_engine_native_tip: Select this to use the built-in solver. Otherwise, the EPANET solver from the US EPA is used. The built-in solver runs every network the page builds, including an extended period simulation and an EPANET-MSX analysis, and the status bar states which solver was used. Input that EPANET does not accept is not accepted by the built-in solver either, and the status bar reports it. The first time the EPANET solver is used, about 650 KB is downloaded and then kept on this device. Where a pipe has a minor (local) loss, the two solvers differ in the last digits: EPANET uses a rounded value of gravitational acceleration, so its minor losses are very slightly lower than the exact form.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_run_stopped: The EPANET run stopped at {time}, so it has no results. The Solver (run) report says why.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_run_stopped_kept: The EPANET run stopped at {time}. Results run to {solved}, the last period it solved, and none are shown after it. The Solver (run) report says why.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_run_fell_back: The numbers on screen came from the built-in solver instead. They show the network at {time} only, with every tank at its initial level.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_epanet_fallback: The EPANET solver could not be loaded, so the built-in solver ran this network.
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_epanet_fallback_why: The built-in solver ran this network, because the EPANET solver could not be used. {reason}
keys_to_translate.lpn_time_run_report_tip: The text report of the last run: the network counts, the analysis options, whether it converged, the status of each step, and any warnings. Its header states the solver used, and both solvers use the layout and wording of the EPANET report.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_demand_model_tip: Choose how junctions receive flow. Demand driven (DDA) delivers every demand in full, whatever the pressure. Pressure driven (PDA) delivers less than the demand where the pressure is below the required pressure.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_rules_refused: EPANET does not accept these rules, because a clause is not valid for the element it names or states a value that cannot be read. Correct or delete them:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_control_refused: EPANET does not accept the controls on these links, because a control cannot act on a check valve, a numeric setting cannot control a general purpose valve, and the setting of a pipe or pump cannot be negative. Correct or delete the controls on:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_rule_step_refused: Rules need a hydraulic time step of at least 10 seconds. EPANET evaluates rules at one tenth of the hydraulic time step, in whole seconds, and a result of 0 cannot run. Increase the hydraulic time step or delete the rules.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_speed_pattern_refused: These pumps use a speed pattern that does not exist or that holds a negative value. A speed pattern must exist and hold values of 0 or more:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_tank_curve_refused: The volume curves of these tanks cannot be used. A curve needs at least two points, each level greater than the one before it, and a range that reaches from the minimum level to the maximum level of the tank:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_tank_levels_refused: The initial level of these tanks is not between the minimum level and the maximum level:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_quality_refused: EPANET does not accept this water quality input: a source type, source pattern or mixing model that does not exist, a quality time step of 0 seconds (a hydraulic time step under 10 seconds with no quality time step stated), or an EPANET-MSX file that cannot be read. Correct these:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_energy_refused: EPANET does not accept this energy input: a negative price or demand charge, an efficiency of 0 or less, a price pattern that does not exist, or an efficiency curve whose flows do not increase. Correct these:

keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_builtin_stopped_at: The built-in solver stopped at {time}, so the run has no results. To run this network with the EPANET solver, change the setting under Calculation, Solver in Settings.

keys.lpn_inpalt_lead: This file changes values in the categories below. Choose the alternative that receives the values of each.
keys.lpn_inpalt_base_note: Every scenario inherits the Base alternative, so choosing it changes them all.
keys.lpn_notes_1_def: By default the network is solved by the EPANET solver. When a total run time is set, each reporting time step is calculated in sequence: tanks fill and drain, demands follow their patterns, and the toolbar plays back the run. With Use the built-in solver selected, the network, including an extended period simulation and an EPANET-MSX analysis, is solved by the built-in solver instead. Input that EPANET does not accept is not accepted by the built-in solver either, and the status bar reports it.
keys.lpn_engine_unavailable: Could not download the EPANET solver, so the built-in solver runs this network. After one connection to the internet, the EPANET solver is stored on this device.
keys.lpn_engine_unavailable_why: The EPANET solver could not be downloaded, so the built-in solver runs this network. {reason}
keys.lpn_engine_needed_failed: The EPANET solver has not yet been loaded and cannot be loaded now, so the built-in solver runs this network. EPANET will be loaded when you are connected to the internet.
keys.lpn_engine_needed_failed_why: The EPANET solver could not be loaded, so the built-in solver runs this network. {reason}
keys.lpn_settings_engine_native_tip: Select this to use the built-in solver. Otherwise, the EPANET solver from the US EPA is used. The built-in solver runs every network the page builds, including an extended period simulation and an EPANET-MSX analysis, and the status bar states which solver was used. Input that EPANET does not accept is not accepted by the built-in solver either, and the status bar reports it. The first time the EPANET solver is used, about 650 KB is downloaded and then kept on this device. Where a pipe has a minor (local) loss, the two solvers differ in the last digits: EPANET uses a rounded value of gravitational acceleration, so its minor losses are very slightly lower than the exact form.
keys.lpn_time_run_stopped: The EPANET run stopped at {time}, so it has no results. The Solver (run) report says why.
keys.lpn_time_run_stopped_kept: The EPANET run stopped at {time}. Results run to {solved}, the last period it solved, and none are shown after it. The Solver (run) report says why.
keys.lpn_time_run_fell_back: The numbers on screen came from the built-in solver instead. They show the network at {time} only, with every tank at its initial level.
keys.lpn_time_epanet_fallback: The EPANET solver could not be loaded, so the built-in solver ran this network.
keys.lpn_time_epanet_fallback_why: The built-in solver ran this network, because the EPANET solver could not be used. {reason}
keys.lpn_time_run_report_tip: The text report of the last run: the network counts, the analysis options, whether it converged, the status of each step, and any warnings. Its header states the solver used, and both solvers use the layout and wording of the EPANET report.
keys.lpn_settings_demand_model_tip: Choose how junctions receive flow. Demand driven (DDA) delivers every demand in full, whatever the pressure. Pressure driven (PDA) delivers less than the demand where the pressure is below the required pressure.
keys.lpn_diag_rules_refused: EPANET does not accept these rules, because a clause is not valid for the element it names or states a value that cannot be read. Correct or delete them:
keys.lpn_diag_control_refused: EPANET does not accept the controls on these links, because a control cannot act on a check valve, a numeric setting cannot control a general purpose valve, and the setting of a pipe or pump cannot be negative. Correct or delete the controls on:
keys.lpn_diag_rule_step_refused: Rules need a hydraulic time step of at least 10 seconds. EPANET evaluates rules at one tenth of the hydraulic time step, in whole seconds, and a result of 0 cannot run. Increase the hydraulic time step or delete the rules.
keys.lpn_diag_speed_pattern_refused: These pumps use a speed pattern that does not exist or that holds a negative value. A speed pattern must exist and hold values of 0 or more:
keys.lpn_diag_tank_curve_refused: The volume curves of these tanks cannot be used. A curve needs at least two points, each level greater than the one before it, and a range that reaches from the minimum level to the maximum level of the tank:
keys.lpn_diag_tank_levels_refused: The initial level of these tanks is not between the minimum level and the maximum level:
keys.lpn_diag_quality_refused: EPANET does not accept this water quality input: a source type, source pattern or mixing model that does not exist, a quality time step of 0 seconds (a hydraulic time step under 10 seconds with no quality time step stated), or an EPANET-MSX file that cannot be read. Correct these:
keys.lpn_diag_energy_refused: EPANET does not accept this energy input: a negative price or demand charge, an efficiency of 0 or less, a price pattern that does not exist, or an efficiency curve whose flows do not increase. Correct these:
keys.lpn_diag_builtin_stopped: The built-in solver stopped, so the run has no results. To run this network with the EPANET solver, change the setting under Calculation, Solver in Settings.
keys.lpn_diag_builtin_stopped_at: The built-in solver stopped at {time}, so the run has no results. To run this network with the EPANET solver, change the setting under Calculation, Solver in Settings.
keys.lpn_diag_builtin_error: An error occurred in the built-in solver: {message}

previous_translated.value: Један фактор који се примењује на сваку потрошњу у мрежи одједном. Сваки сценарио може имати засебну вредност, па се просечан дан, максималан дан или врхунски час могу направити променом само овог подешавања.

next_translated.value: Укључите ово да бисте, где је могуће, користили уграђени решавач. У супротном, увек се користи EPANET решавач америчке агенције EPA. Уграђени решавач се не користи за симулације током продуженог периода. При првом коришћењу EPANET решавача преузима се око 650 KB, који потом остаје сачуван на овом уређају. Где цев има локални (минорни) губитак, два решавача се разилазе у последњим цифрама: EPANET користи заокружену вредност гравитационог убрзања, па су његови локални губици веома благо нижи него у тачном облику.
next_translated.english: Select this to use the built-in solver. Otherwise, the EPANET solver from the US EPA is used. The built-in solver runs every network the page builds, including an extended period simulation and an EPANET-MSX analysis, and the status bar states which solver was used. Input that EPANET does not accept is not accepted by the built-in solver either, and the status bar reports it. The first time the EPANET solver is used, about 650 KB is downloaded and then kept on this device. Where a pipe has a minor (local) loss, the two solvers differ in the last digits: EPANET uses a rounded value of gravitational acceleration, so its minor losses are very slightly lower than the exact form.

Tucked away, the box shows only the start of its title, on a narrow tab at the map's edge turned on its side, cut off after about 12 to 25 characters. Put the word that names the box's subject first, so each tab can be told from its neighbors; a title form with a colon is fine (Pump energy report, in Spanish: Bombas: informe de energía). Where the natural phrase already starts with that word, keep it. The same text may also be a menu row.
